newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's effectively frees internal coffee price.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's effectively frees internal coffee price.

text.p: Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said Thursday that Colombia's official internal coffee price had effectively been tossed out the window.

Ocampo, who spoke in an interview with the Radionet news program, said the National Coffee Growers' Federation had been authorized to pay any price necessary to supply itself with fresh coffee to meet its export commitments.

"We authorize the federation to buy at higher prices," Ocampo said, explaining that the move would allow the federation to compete on an equal footing with private exporters for the scarce amount of coffee currently available on the Colombian market.
The federation's general manager, Jorge Cardenas, said Monday the federation was having "enormous difficulties" meeting its export commitments because of unusually tight supply.

Cardenas also complained that 125-kg loads of coffee were being sold to private exporters in some parts of the country for more than 400,000 pesos, while the federation was obliged to pay no more than the official internal price, which was set last Friday at 388,375 pesos.
"The federation has been left without fresh coffee," Ocampo said. "They have coffee in stocks but part of the commitments, the majority, have to be fulfilled with fresh coffee."
Cardenas acknowledged in his remarks to reporters Monday that the federation had fallen behind on its coffee export schedules for April because of a shortfall in production.
The federation's coffee inventories currently stand at about 4.8 million 60-kg bags, according to official figures.

But one exporter told Reuters that figures obtained from federation sources showed that its stocks of fresh coffee amounted to just 800,000 bags, with the remainder being old crop coffee from 1991 to 1995 or beans affected by the berry borer plague. ((-- Juan Guillermo Londono, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944))
